component.name: Gearbench
component.summary: Settings for the Logitech G915, G502 X PLUS, G305 and Astro A50 Gen 4

description.p: Gearbench is a control panel for the Logitech G915 keyboard, the G502 X PLUS and G305 mice, and the Astro A50 Gen 4 headset with its base station's switch on PC. Only these models attach, the A50's Xbox edition not among them, and another is added once it has been tested on the hardware. It talks to the keyboard and mice over their vendor HID++ 2.0 interfaces, on a cable or through a LIGHTSPEED receiver, and to the headset's base station over its own vendor HID interface, with no vendor software and nothing running as root. For each device it shows only what that device can do.

ul.li: Per-key and zone lighting, with the six effects the firmware has
G1 to G5 bound to key combinations or macros, on the base layer and, from gearbench-ctl, the MR shift layer
Three M profiles, switched by the M1 to M3 keys
Backlight brightness, snapped to a level the firmware keeps
DPI set live and remembered per model, and the onboard DPI stage list and report rate rewritten
On the G502 X PLUS, G4 to G9 bound to key combinations, macros, DPI shift, DPI up and down, or the browser buttons
Lighting where the mouse has it, either its own or following the keyboard
Microphone level, sidetone, noise gate and mic EQ
The three EQ presets, edited band by band or imported from Astro Command Center's files
The stream port mix, the base station's own settings and the headset's battery
Changes apply at once; Save writes them to the base station's flash, and until then Revert to saved undoes all of them but Auto shut-off and which preset is active
Game and Chat as two outputs, and Astro A50 Spatial, a 7.1 output for games, rendered for headphones from measured heads

description.p: Game profiles hold a lighting and binding set that loads itself while a named program's window has focus, and macros are recorded from the Macros tab and replayed through a uinput virtual keyboard and mouse.

Lighting is volatile and the keyboard's onboard profile is never written. Each write to the mouse's onboard profile, from the window or gearbench-ctl, backs up every profile sector first and reads the written sector back after.
A security policy says how to report a security problem privately.
